biography: Alexandre Sebastia, a name whispered with a mix of respect and apprehension in the Superkart 250cc circuit, hails from the small town of Charleville-Mézières in the Ardennes region of France. His journey began not on the tarmac, but amidst the winding forest trails of the Ardennes, where he honed his reflexes navigating dirt bikes with his father, a former enduro racer. The transition to karting was almost accidental; a birthday gift at age 14 revealed an innate talent for speed and precision. His defining moment came at the 2018 European Superkart Championship in Assen, where he secured his first major victory, overcoming a mid-race mechanical issue and a relentless challenge from veteran racer Marco Vitale. Now at 28, Sebastia is considered to be entering his peak, a calculating force to be reckoned with, perpetually seeking the slightest advantage on the track. He is known for his meticulous preparation and ice-cold demeanor under pressure.
drivingStyle: Sebastia is known for his exceptionally smooth and calculated driving style. He prioritizes corner entry speed, often sacrificing a bit of exit acceleration to maintain momentum. Tire management is a hallmark of his approach; he is masterful at preserving rubber throughout a race, allowing him to push harder in the final laps when others are struggling. Under pressure, he remains remarkably composed, rarely making rash decisions and preferring to exploit the mistakes of others rather than forcing an overtake.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Superkart World Championship in Le Mans, France, on home soil, after a nail-biting final lap overtake to secure the title, fulfilling a lifelong dream.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final round of the 2019 European Championship due to a rare mechanical failure, costing him the championship title and leading to doubts about his team's reliability.
